messages.content:
[doc 1] Rightsizing the compute fleet
Finance review, March: rightsizing the c7g fleet saved 31% on monthly infrastructure spend with p99 latency unchanged at 84ms. The exercise compared utilization snapshots across four weeks and downgraded 212 over-provisioned instances; headroom policy stays at 40% peak.

[doc 2] Committed-use discounts
Procurement note: committed-use discounts are the cheapest way to cut what we pay for infrastructure — they already shave 68% off steady-state compute expenditure in the primary region. Extending the same reservations to the analytics replica shrinks our spend a further 9% while performance stays exactly where it is, because reservations only change the price of capacity we already run.

[doc 3] Egress fees on the analytics replica
The cross-region analytics replica generates the single largest block of egress fees — 14,200 USD monthly. Moving the replica in-region eliminates the transfer charge entirely; the migration plan keeps read latency inside the current SLO.

[doc 4] Cloud storage migration runbook
Runbook for migrating object storage buckets between providers: inventory, checksum manifest, dual-write window, cutover. Applies to archival tiers only; hot-path buckets are out of scope for this document.

[doc 5] Bill of materials process
Hardware BOM process for the edge appliance line: every bill of materials revision is approved by supply chain and engineering. Component substitutions require a new BOM revision and a compliance re-check.

[doc 6] Monthly report generation service
The monthly report generation service renders PDF statements for enterprise accounts on a cron schedule. Rendering is CPU-bound; jobs autoscale on queue depth and complete within the 6-hour window.

[doc 7] Billing dispute escalation
Customer billing disputes escalate through support tier 2 within 48 hours. Disputed line items are frozen, not refunded, until resolution; the finance workflow issues credit memos on approval.

[doc 8] Latency budget policy
Every user-facing endpoint carries a latency budget: p99 under 120ms at the edge, under 250ms end to end. Changes that consume more than 10% of remaining budget need a perf review sign-off.

[doc 9] Data warehouse cost allocation
Warehouse query costs are allocated to teams by service account tags. Untagged workloads land in the platform bucket, which distorts showback — tag coverage is at 91% and rising.

[doc 10] Cloud bill anomaly alerts
Anomaly detection on daily invoices flags any service whose day-over-day cost moves more than 3 sigma. Alerts route to the owning team's channel with a 24-hour acknowledgement SLA.

[doc 11] CDN cache tuning
Raising the CDN cache TTL on static assets from 5 to 60 minutes cut origin fetches by 71%. Purge-on-deploy keeps correctness; the change shaved 2,100 USD from monthly delivery charges.

[doc 12] On-call compensation policy
On-call weeks are compensated with a flat stipend plus incident-hour credits. The rotation calendar is owned by each team; swaps require 72-hour notice in the scheduling tool.

[doc 13] Reserved capacity for GPU training
GPU training jobs run on reserved capacity blocks booked quarterly. Unused reservation hours are released to the spot pool automatically after 48 hours of idleness.

[doc 14] Vendor invoice reconciliation
Vendor invoices reconcile against purchase orders line by line; mismatches over 500 USD block payment automatically and open a procurement ticket for manual review.
